Specification: This module specifies a solution to the classic prisoners-and-switches puzzle. One designated prisoner acts as a counter, while every other prisoner is allowed to move switch A up at most twice; the counter increments a count whenever he finds switch A up and turns it down, and everyone otherwise flips switch B. The specification models random repeated selection of prisoners under weak fairness assumptions that guarantee the counter and every non-counter prisoner are brought into the room infinitely often, and it states both a safety property saying that when the protocol declares completion then every prisoner has visited the room, and a liveness property saying that the declaration condition is eventually reached.
IfThenElse:
IF (~switchAUp) /\ (timesSwitched[i] < 2)
       THEN /\ switchAUp' = TRUE
            /\ timesSwitched' = [timesSwitched EXCEPT ![i] = @+1]
            /\ UNCHANGED switchBUp
       ELSE /\ switchBUp' = ~switchBUp
            /\ UNCHANGED <<switchAUp, timesSwitched>>

IF switchAUp
       THEN /\ switchAUp' = FALSE
            /\ UNCHANGED switchBUp
            /\ count' =  count + 1
       ELSE /\ switchBUp' = ~switchBUp
            /\ UNCHANGED <<switchAUp, count>>

IF S = {} THEN 0
                        ELSE LET p == CHOOSE pr \in S : TRUE
                             IN  timesSwitched[p] + sum[S \ {p}]

Fairness is classified as a StatePredicate by the prompt's structural rule because its body contains no primed variables and no explicit [], <>, or ~>; it consists of fairness operators WF_vars(...), which are temporal in meaning but not part of the requested TemporalProperty trigger.
CountInvariant is classified as a StatePredicate because its body is Boolean-valued and contains no primed variables or temporal operators.
PostCondition is classified as a StatePredicate by elimination: it is a Boolean-valued operator with empty body text in the source.
CounterExample is classified as a ValueDef by elimination: it defines a non-Boolean structured value (a record containing action and state data).
Safety is placed in TemporalProperty because its body has [] at the outermost level.
Spec is placed in TemporalProperty because it contains the temporal formula [][Next]_vars at top level.
